sections.title: What you can spend today
body: Enter a monthly budget, and the money left is divided by the days left to show what you can spend each day. When you spend, the daily amount is worked out again. When there is something to flag, such as going over budget or using up what is left, one line below tells you. With a daily budget, what is left for today shows in large numbers.

sections.title: Choose the days that count
body: Every day counts by default. Turn on Count Weekdays Only to leave out weekends, plus Korean public holidays if your iPhone's region is South Korea. To leave out a day you won't spend, tap it in the calendar. With a monthly budget, the daily amount is then divided again over the days left. Past days in the calendar show what you spent. Tap a day with a recorded merchant to see where you spent, or touch and hold a past day or today to add a payment on that date.

sections.title: Set it up for your budget
body: By default it helps you stay within budget. With a monthly budget, money left at the end of a period is added to the next period's budget. If the money disappears when the period ends, as with welfare points or a grant, set Leftover Handling to Expires. Then nothing carries over, and it tells you to use it all in time. Choose the day your budget starts, from the 1st to the 28th. The money left also shows in Home Screen and Lock Screen widgets.

sections.title: Recording payments
body: You can add any payment by hand. If your iPhone's region is South Korea, you can also record card payments from messages. If card payments reach you by text message, you can set up a Shortcuts automation to record them without opening the app. If they come through a card app or KakaoTalk, paste the notice or enter the amount yourself. Enter a card's last 4 digits to record only that card's messages, or leave them empty to record payment messages from every card.

sections.title: When the balance is off
body: If the record and your real balance differ, tap the big number and enter the real amount. One Balance adjustment line records the difference, and your original transactions stay as they are.

a: Choose a monthly or daily budget, enter one amount, and tap Start. There is no account or login.

If you start a monthly budget partway through a period, enter the real amount left in the Money Left This Month field (Money Left This Period if the period doesn't start on the 1st). If you leave it empty, the full budget is used. If your iPhone region is South Korea, enter your card's last 4 digits under Payment Notices. The period start day, Count weekdays only and Leftover Handling are under More Options, and you can change them later in Settings.

Every day counts by default. If the money isn't for weekends, turn on Count Weekdays Only in Settings. Weekends are left out, plus public holidays if your iPhone's region is South Korea. To leave out a specific day, tap it in the calendar on the main screen. When the calendar is collapsed it shows only this week, so tap Expand Calendar to reach other weeks. You can't leave out past days. Once a day you left out has passed, its Out mark goes away and it counts like any other day.

For the South Korea region, public holidays for 2026 to 2028 are built into the app, and later years are added in app updates. 2028 was worked out from the Korea Astronomy and Space Science Institute calendar data and will be checked again once the official dates are published. In years not on the list, only weekends are left out. Tap any temporary holiday that isn't on the list to leave it out in the calendar.

faq.q: Money left at the end of a period
a: With a monthly budget, money left when a period ends is added to the next period's budget. Only money left over carries over, and spending over budget is not taken from the next period. When money has carried over, the line under the bar on the main screen also shows the amount carried over from last period. The first time you open the app in a new period, a short notice also shows how much carried over. Carry-over starts from the period you first set up, or the period where you set Leftover Handling to Carries Over or switched to Monthly Budget. Changing the budget amount or start day after that does not recalculate money that has already carried over. A daily budget does not carry over.

If the money disappears when unspent, as with welfare points or a grant, set Leftover Handling to Expires under More Rules in Settings. Nothing carries over then, and the app tells you to use it all within the period.

faq.q: Daily budgets and the calculation period
a: To budget by the day, change the budget type in Settings to Daily Budget. A new share appears on each counted day, and days that don't count have no share.

If your budget doesn't start on the 1st, open Calculation Period in Settings and pick a start day from the 1st to the 28th under Monthly. With DailyLeft Pro you can also pick the 29th, the 30th, Last Day, Move Earlier on Weekends and Holidays, Weekly, Every 2 Weeks and Pick Dates (a length of 2 to 92 days that repeats). When you change the calculation period, past records are split into the new periods too, and periods from before the change show only what you spent. If the type of period changes, you enter the amount again, and carried-over money counts again from 0 that day.

faq.q: The daily amount on a day you pay
a: With a monthly budget, if today is a counted day and you have a payment today, today's count ends and the money left is divided again from tomorrow. The screen shows Done for today. If you cancel every payment that day, today counts again. Balance adjustments don't count as payments.

faq.q: How the daily amount is rounded
a: In won, the daily amount in the big number, the status line and the widgets is rounded down to the hundred by default, so 18,383 won shows as 18,300 won. With a monthly budget, choose 1,000, 100, 10 or 1 won in Daily Amount Unit under More Rules in Settings. Amounts under the unit you chose stay as they are, and when one day is left the whole amount left shows. The total left and transaction amounts are not rounded. Other currencies are not rounded by default, and you can pick a unit for them in the same place.

faq.q: Recording text messages with a Shortcuts automation (South Korea)
a: This works only if your iPhone's region was South Korea when you first set up the app. Elsewhere, use Add by Hand. If payment notices reach you by text message, you can set up a Shortcuts automation. Automation Setup, opened from Shortcuts Automation in Settings, has Get Shortcut, which gets you a shortcut with the single app action Record Payment Message through a link. You add the shortcut in the Shortcuts app and turn on the automation yourself. The steps for your iOS version are listed in order on the same screen. If the link doesn't open, follow the steps under Build It Yourself, which starts collapsed. Once the automation has run, the Shortcuts Automation row in Settings shows Working. When the automation records a payment, a silent one-line notification arrives instead of a result window. Messages from other cards and messages that aren't payments don't send one. If you haven't allowed notifications yet, tap Allow Notifications in Automation Setup; if they're turned off, turn them on with Open Settings.

The app can't read your Messages directly. It reads only text passed by the automation or text you paste. The automation's Contains field decides which messages are passed. With only 승인 (approved) there, cancellation messages may not be recorded. To catch those too, put your card's last 4 digits in that field.

faq.q: Card app notices and KakaoTalk notices
a: iOS limits mean the app can't read card app notices or KakaoTalk notices automatically. Copy the notice and paste it into Add from Message, or use Add by Hand. In Add from Message, tapping Paste records a notice the app can read right away. Add from Message appears only for the South Korea region.

If you enter them, only messages from the card with those last 4 digits are recorded. If you leave them empty, payment messages from every card are recorded. In that case, messages with a readable date, time and amount are recorded, and messages containing the Korean words for deposit, withdrawal, transfer, loan, billing or statement are not recorded. Messages containing the Korean words for declined, failed, not possible, insufficient balance or over the limit count as declined and are never recorded, with or without the card digits.

faq.q: If a message isn't recorded (South Korea)
a: Check that the automation's Message Text field holds the trigger's Message. If you entered your card's last 4 digits, a message must show those 4 digits in full to be read. For other messages, empty the card field or use Add by Hand.

Messages are read using the Hana Card format as the base, and other card companies' messages are read by finding the amount, date and last 4 digits. Messages with no date or time can't be read, and payments not in won are not recorded.

If Add from Message can't read a message, Report Message appears under the result. Tap it to open a mail draft with the original text. You can delete or change the name, merchant or card number before sending. You send it yourself from your own mail app.
Reported messages are used only to teach the app that format and to reply to you.

Tap the big number or Adjust Balance and enter the real amount. One Balance adjustment line records the difference, and your original transactions stay as they are. Swipe in the list to delete adjustment lines and transactions.
To enter a cancellation or refund by hand, turn on Cancellation or Refund in Add by Hand.
Home Screen widgets come in small and medium sizes. They show the money left and what you can spend today, and the medium size also lists your 3 latest transactions.

There are three Lock Screen widgets. The rectangular one shows the money left and what you can spend today, the circular one shows the share left, and the inline one shows the money left. Until you enter a budget in the app, they show Not set up or a question mark.

With DailyLeft Pro and two or more budgets, the Budgets widget shows what's left in each budget at a glance. It comes in small, medium and large on the Home Screen and in the three Lock Screen shapes, and you choose Budgets to Show when you edit the widget. In the medium and large sizes, tapping a budget opens the app on that budget. The original widget always shows the first budget.
Ads appear in one banner spot at the bottom of the main screen.

faq.q: DailyLeft Pro and restoring a purchase
a: Tap DailyLeft Pro at the top of Settings to see what Pro includes and its price, then tap Buy Pro. The same screen opens when you tap a Pro spot such as Add Budget, a Pro option in Calculation Period, Period Wrap-up on a past period, or a Balance Alerts switch. After you buy, the ad banner on the main screen goes away, and the ad consent form and the tracking prompt stop appearing.

If you bought Remove Ads before, DailyLeft Pro is already on after the update. If you switch devices or reinstall the app, tap Restore Purchases under Info in Settings. With the same Apple Account you won't pay again.

If Pro turns off after a refund or when Family Sharing ends, the budgets you made, the calculation period you chose and your records stay and keep counting. Only adding a budget, choosing another Pro period type, Period Wrap-up and Balance Alerts stop working.

With DailyLeft Pro you can keep up to 4 budgets, each with its own amount, calculation period and leftover handling. Add one with Add Budget in Settings. The first time, you also name the budget you've been using. With two or more budgets, switch between them in the row at the top of the main screen. There is no combined total across budgets.

If your iPhone region is South Korea, a payment message goes to the budget whose card last 4 digits match, and if none match, to the budget with the last 4 digits left empty. Only one budget can have them empty, and the same last 4 digits can't go in two budgets. Make one automation per card number. You only need Get Shortcut once. If a budget has no last 4 digits, or on iOS 27, one automation with 승인 takes messages for every budget. Either way the app picks the right budget for each message, and the steps are under Shortcuts Automation in Settings.
From the second budget on, delete a budget with Delete Budget on its screen. All of its records are deleted too and can't be brought back. The first budget can't be deleted.

With DailyLeft Pro, a past period shows a Period Wrap-up under the big number: what you spent and the number of payments, the daily average, the biggest day, the top place, the money carried over, left unspent or over budget, and the change from the period before. It doesn't appear for a period with no payments.

Turn on Balance under 10% and Over today's amount under Balance Alerts in Settings. The first time, iOS asks whether to allow notifications. You get one alert when a recorded payment crosses the line, and a daily budget only gets Over today's amount. If you didn't allow notifications, turn on DailyLeft notifications in the iOS Settings app.
If you see an ad that's inappropriate or unsuitable for the app's age rating, email kvndh36@naver.com with when it appeared and what it showed. The developer will review it and block it in AdMob.

iOS asks whether to allow tracking after you tap Start on the first-run screen. You can use the app the same way if you don't allow it, and you can change this choice in iOS Settings > Privacy & Security > Tracking.
Where ad consent is required, such as the European Economic Area, the consent form appears before the tracking prompt. In those places you can change your consent from Privacy Choices in Settings.

Budget calculations, recording, widgets and balance alerts work without a connection. Ads, buying DailyLeft Pro, Restore Purchases, the iCloud backup, sending a report email and opening the privacy policy need a connection.

If you're signed in to iCloud and iCloud Backup is on in Settings, a backup of your records is kept in your own iCloud. If you delete and reinstall the app, or install it on another iPhone with the same Apple Account, the records come back from that backup before you set the app up. It is not a sync that keeps two devices matched, and a device that already has records is never overwritten.

iPhone only, with iOS 26 or later. The app's screens are in 46 languages. It uses the first language in your device's language list that the app supports, or English if none is supported. Portrait and landscape are supported. Amounts are whole numbers in your region's currency, set when you first set up the app. There are no decimals or exchange rates, so you can't enter 12.50. Recording from messages takes only payments in won.
Close the app fully, open it again, and check the App Store for the latest version. If the problem continues, email us with the screen you were on and what you were doing.

privacy.title: DailyLeft Privacy Policy
privacy.summary: The app's records are saved in a file on your device, and the developer does not receive that file. If you're signed in to iCloud and iCloud Backup is on in Settings, a backup of the same records is also kept in your own iCloud so they can come back when you reinstall the app, and the developer does not receive that backup either. If you choose to send a message report email, the developer receives it. It is used only to teach the app that message format and to reply. It is deleted without delay after the developer decides whether to add that format to the app, and at most 1 year after it was received. Banner ads come from Google AdMob, which processes device information such as the advertising identifier. Apple handles payment for DailyLeft Pro and restoring it. Balance alerts and the record notifications from a Shortcuts automation are notifications this iPhone makes and shows, and the developer does not receive their contents.
intro: kvndh ("the developer") handles the personal information of people who use the DailyLeft app ("the app") under Korea's Personal Information Protection Act, as set out below.

sections.title: Purpose of processing
paragraphs: The app has no sign-up or login. It uses the budget and payment records you enter to work out the money left and what you can spend today. These records are in a saved file on your device, and the developer does not receive that file. If you're signed in to iCloud and iCloud Backup is on in Settings, a backup of these records is also kept in your own iCloud (section 8), and the developer does not receive that backup either.
The app shows a banner ad at the bottom of the main screen. Google's ad service AdMob selects and displays that ad, and uses device information to show ads and measure how they perform.
If you send a message report email, the developer receives it. The developer uses it to teach the app that card company's message format and to reply to you, and for no other purpose.

sections.title: Information processed
paragraphs: The data the app saves on your device is listed at the end of this section. Of these, the budget settings, card last 4 digits, transactions, original message text and the budget list also go into the iCloud backup (section 8). The developer does not receive it. The app does not receive contacts, location or photos.

The app can't read your Messages directly. It reads only text passed by a Shortcuts automation you made or text you paste. You decide in the Shortcuts app which messages are passed. Text that is read but not recorded is not saved. These message features appear only for the South Korea region.

If you send a message report email, the developer receives your email address, the original message text you chose to send (which may include part of the approver's name, the merchant, the card's last 4 digits, the amount and the time), the reason it could not be read, the app and iOS versions, and information your mail app adds (such as your sender name, depending on your mail account settings). The app does not send this email. You send it yourself from your own mail app, and you can delete or change it before sending.
Information that AdMob may collect when showing ads is listed in section 9.
bullets: Budget settings (budget type, currency and amount, period start day, the calculation period rule and the day it was last changed, Count weekdays only, Leftover Handling, Daily Amount Unit, the day carry-over started counting and the money carried into that period, whether payments go through over budget, how payment notices arrive, days left out in the calendar): used to work out the money left and the daily amount, kept separately for each budget if you use several
Card last 4 digits (if entered, for each budget): used to record a payment message to the right budget and skip messages from other cards
Transactions (date, amount, merchant or memo, time added to the app, how it was recorded): used to work out the money left and for the transaction list

The original text of recorded payment messages: saved as is in the saved file and used so the same message isn't recorded twice. It may include part of the approver's name (for example H*D), the merchant, the card's last 4 digits, the amount and the time
The budget list (if you added budgets with DailyLeft Pro: budget names and an internal ID the app assigns): used to tell budgets apart and show their names

The last balance seen and when (for each budget), the budget last viewed, when a notice about a record in another budget was last shown, a first-run mark, the day a celebration was shown, and whether the calendar is expanded: used to draw the screen
When the Shortcuts automation last ran and whether the message text it passed was empty: used to show under Shortcuts Automation in Settings whether the automation is working

Whether you have DailyLeft Pro (including an earlier Remove Ads purchase) and whether to show a one-time note that an earlier purchase now counts as Pro: used to open Pro features, hide the banner and skip the ad consent check, the tracking prompt and the ad SDK start
Whether balance alerts are on (Balance under 10%, Over today's amount): used to decide whether to send an alert after a payment is recorded

iCloud backup state (a random value the app creates to tell this installation apart, whether it is linked to the backup, when it last restored from the backup): used so the app doesn't overwrite or delete a backup another device uploaded

sections.title: Processing and retention period
paragraphs: Records on your device stay until you delete them or delete the app. Delete a transaction by swiping it in the list. If no other app from the developer that uses the same App Group is on the device, deleting the app removes the records and settings with it. A budget added with DailyLeft Pro takes its records with it when you delete the budget.
The iCloud backup stays in your iCloud even after you delete the app, so it can be used when you install the app again.
A message report email is deleted without delay after the developer decides whether to add that message format to the app, and at most 1 year after it was received.
Information collected by AdMob is kept as set out in Google's Privacy Policy (policies.google.com/privacy).

sections.title: Disclosure to third parties
paragraphs: The developer does not provide users' personal information or message report emails to third parties. However, the Google Mobile Ads SDK and Google User Messaging Platform SDK built into the app send the information in section 9 directly to Google, as follows.
bullets: Recipient: Google LLC (United States), AdMob
Purpose: checking ad consent, showing ads and measuring ad performance
Information: the device information and ad interaction records listed in section 9
When and how: sent over the internet when the app opens, checks consent and starts the SDK, and when an ad is loaded and shown
Retention: as set out in Google's Privacy Policy

Level of protection: Google complies with applicable data protection law under the Google Ads Controller-Controller Data Protection Terms. The developer lets information go only to third parties that provide the same or equal protection as this policy

sections.title: Outsourcing of processing
paragraphs: The developer does not outsource the processing of personal information. Apple processes payment for DailyLeft Pro and Restore Purchases through the App Store, and payment information is governed by Apple's privacy policy. The developer does not receive your payment method or Apple Account details.
A message report email travels through your mail service to the developer's Naver mailbox (kvndh36@naver.com).

sections.title: Destruction of information
paragraphs: Records on your device are removed when you delete them from the transaction list or delete the app. From the second budget on, Delete Budget deletes that budget's record file.

The iCloud backup stays in your own iCloud even after you delete the app, and installing the app again with the same Apple Account brings the records back. If you turn off iCloud Backup in the app's Settings and save, the app deletes the backup in iCloud and stops uploading. If you turn it on again, it uploads the records at that time.
A message report email is deleted from the mailbox without delay after the developer decides whether to add that message format to the app, and at most 1 year after it was received.

sections.title: Rights of users and legal guardians, and how to exercise them
paragraphs: If you have sent a message report email, you can ask to view or delete that email at the address below. If you have questions, email us at the same address.
You can check and delete the records on your device yourself in the app.
The iCloud backup is kept in your own Apple Account, so the developer cannot view or delete it.
You can ask Google to give you access to, or delete, information collected by AdMob (policies.google.com/privacy). To refuse use of the advertising identifier, follow section 9.

sections.title: Security measures
paragraphs: The first budget's records and settings sit in a file (ledger.json) in storage the app and its widgets share on your device (an App Group). If you add budgets with DailyLeft Pro, a budget list (cards.json) and one file per budget appear in the same place. The widgets only read these files and do not use the ad SDK. Values used to draw the screen are in the app's UserDefaults, and whether you have DailyLeft Pro and whether balance alerts are on are in the settings of the same App Group (the purchase state also has a copy in the app's UserDefaults). The developer runs no server. If you're signed in to iCloud and iCloud Backup is on in Settings, the app compresses all of these records and backs them up to the key-value storage of your own iCloud. With two or more budgets, records from the second budget on and the budget list go into a separate backup entry, and if the two entries together would go over the iCloud limit, that entry isn't uploaded and Settings says so. It is not a sync between devices, and the app restores from the backup only when setup isn't finished on the device and it has no transactions. These files can also be included in iCloud device backups or Mac backups you turn on.

The app does not send email itself. Tapping Report Message only fills in the recipient, subject and body of a mail draft, and you tap send or cancel. If no mail account is set up, it opens a mail app you choose with the same content.

The app asks for two permissions: tracking (ATT) and notifications. It asks for notifications when you turn on Balance Alerts in DailyLeft Pro or tap Allow Notifications in Automation Setup, and once when you open the app if you used a Shortcuts automation up to version 1.1.0. It does not ask for photos, location, camera or contacts. Balance alerts and the record notifications from a Shortcuts automation are made on this iPhone right after a payment is recorded and do not use a developer server or a push service. An alert includes amounts and the balance, plus the budget name if you use several budgets, and whether it shows on the Lock Screen follows your iOS notification settings. The app takes clipboard text only when you paste it. Apart from ads, the only outside addresses the app opens are the message report email, this privacy policy page and the iCloud shortcut link behind Get Shortcut, and only when you tap them.
What the app passes to the ad SDK is the ad request and the banner size. It does not pass budgets, transactions, messages or card numbers.

sections.title: Automatic collection and how to refuse it
paragraphs: The app does not use cookies or analytics tools. It includes the Google Mobile Ads SDK (AdMob) and the Google User Messaging Platform SDK for advertising, which may collect the information below when they check ad consent and when they load and show ads. The list below is what the privacy manifests of the two SDKs declare.

The app checks ad consent information after you tap Start on the first-run screen. If you have already started, it checks when the app opens. Where ad consent is required, such as the European Economic Area, Google's consent form appears first. If ads can be requested and you haven't answered yet, iOS shows the App Tracking Transparency (ATT) prompt. If you don't allow tracking, AdMob does not get the advertising identifier (IDFA), and ads keep appearing. You can change this choice in iOS Settings > Privacy & Security > Tracking.
If the consent result means ads can't be requested, the tracking prompt is not shown and ads are not requested. Where consent is required, change it from Privacy Choices in Settings.

After you buy DailyLeft Pro (or if you bought Remove Ads before), the app checks your purchase when it opens and then skips the consent check, the tracking prompt and the SDK start, and ads are not requested. If you buy while the app is open, the banner goes away at once, but an SDK that has already started stays until you quit the app.
bullets: Device identifiers, and the advertising identifier (IDFA) if you allow tracking
Approximate location
Ad interaction records such as impressions and taps, and app usage records
App performance, crash and diagnostic information

sections.title: Privacy officer
paragraphs: If you have questions about personal information, email us at the address below.

sections.title: Remedies for privacy concerns
paragraphs: If you need advice about a privacy concern or help settling a dispute, you can contact the Korean bodies listed below. If you live outside Korea, you can also contact the data protection authority in your country.
bullets: Personal Information Dispute Mediation Committee: 1833-6972 in Korea (www.kopico.go.kr)
Personal Information Infringement Report Center: 118 in Korea (privacy.kisa.or.kr)
Supreme Prosecutors' Office: 1301 in Korea (www.spo.go.kr)
National Police Agency: 182 in Korea (ecrm.police.go.kr)
European Union and EEA: the data protection authority of your country (edpb.europa.eu)
United Kingdom: Information Commissioner's Office (ico.org.uk)
United States: Federal Trade Commission (reportfraud.ftc.gov)
Other countries: the data protection or consumer protection authority where you live

sections.title: Changes to this policy
paragraphs: If this policy changes, this page will show what changed and the new effective date.

2026-11-19: In version 1.1.1, payments recorded by a Shortcuts automation arrive as a one-line notification, so when the app asks for notification permission and how record notifications are handled were added to the summary and the security measures. The previous effective date was 2026-11-18.

2026-11-18: For DailyLeft Pro in version 1.1.0, the budget list and per-budget record files, the calculation period rule, balance alert settings and the notification permission, and iCloud backup state values were added to the sections on the information processed, retention, deletion and security measures, and the Remove Ads product was renamed DailyLeft Pro. The previous effective date was 2026-11-12.
